---
title: cache
description: "Static cache facade for configured drivers, fail-soft fallback, tag support, and test driver injection."
---

<ApiBadge type="facade" />
<ApiBadge type="cache" />
<ApiBadge type="driver-backed" />
<ApiBadge type="fail-soft" />

Static entry point for cache operations. Resolves the configured driver on first use and reuses it for the process lifetime. Falls back to a secondary driver when the primary cannot be created.

```txt
Symbol: Skim\Cache\Cache
Source: src/Cache/Cache.php
Lifecycle: static facade, driver resolved on first cache call
Drivers: array, file, redis
Fallback: cache.fallback when cache.driver cannot be created
Test seam: setDriver(), reset()
```

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
$user = Cache::remember("user:{$id}", 3600, fn() => User::find($id));
Cache::flush('user:'); // Invalidate all user:* keys
Cache::flushAll();    // Wipe everything
```
</CodeExample>

<WarningBox>

flushAll() clears the entire active cache backend

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

flush() requires a non-empty prefix

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Prefer prefix-based invalidation such as flush('user:') in production

</WarningBox>

## Architecture

<LifecycleFlow>

```txt
Cache::remember() / get() / set() / has()
-> driver()
-> cached driver instance?
-> resolveDriver()
-> makeDriver(config cache.driver)
-> on failure makeDriver(config cache.fallback)
-> concrete driver operation
-> Profiler::cache(...)
```

</LifecycleFlow>

The facade keeps cache usage stable while backend selection remains in config/cache.php. The flush()/flushAll() split forces callers to explicitly choose between targeted and destructive invalidation.

<NoteBox>

The resolved driver is process-local. If tests change cache config at runtime, call reset() before the next cache operation.

</NoteBox>

## Driver Model

<div class="driver-grid">
  <ScopeBox name="array" mutable>
    In-memory cache driver. Values exist only for the current process and are not persisted.
  </ScopeBox>
  <ScopeBox name="file" mutable>
    Filesystem-backed cache driver. Values are persisted on disk.
  </ScopeBox>
  <ScopeBox name="redis" mutable>
    Redis-backed cache driver. Required for tag-scoped cache operations through Cache::tags().
  </ScopeBox>
</div>

## Read API

<ApiMethod name="remember">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function remember(string $key, int $ttl, callable $default): mixed
```

</ApiSignature>

Returns the cached value when the key exists. On a miss, executes the callback, stores the returned value with the provided TTL, records the miss in profiler, and returns the computed value.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key. Use stable prefixes such as user:42 or posts:published so related entries can be invalidated by prefix.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$ttl" type="int" required>

Time to live in seconds for the computed value.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$default" type="callable" required>

Callback executed only when the key is missing or expired.

</ApiParam>

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
$posts = Cache::remember('posts:published', 3600, fn() => Post::published()->get());
```
</CodeExample>

<NoteBox>

Use remember() for expensive reads when recomputing the value on cache miss is safe and deterministic.

</NoteBox>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="get">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function get(string $key, mixed $default = null): mixed
```

</ApiSignature>

Returns the cached value for the key. If the key is missing or expired, returns $default. Each read records a profiler cache event with hit or miss status.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to read.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$default" type="mixed">

Fallback value returned when the key is missing or expired.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="has">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function has(string $key): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Returns true when the active driver contains a non-expired value for the key.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to test.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Write API

<ApiMethod name="set">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function set(string $key, mixed $value, ?int $ttl = null): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Stores a value in the active driver. When $ttl is null, the facade uses cache.ttl from config and falls back to 3600 seconds when that value is not set.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to write.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$value" type="mixed" required>

Value to store. Must be supported by the active driver.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$ttl" type="?int">

Optional TTL in seconds. null means use the configured default TTL.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="delete">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function delete(string $key): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Removes one exact cache key from the active driver and records the delete operation in profiler.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Exact cache key to remove.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Invalidation

<ApiMethod name="flush">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function flush(string $prefix): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Removes keys that match the given prefix. The prefix is required — callers who want a full cache wipe must use flushAll().

<ApiParam name="$prefix" type="string" required>

Key prefix to match. Use a non-empty prefix like user: for safer invalidation.

</ApiParam>

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
Cache::flush('user:'); // Removes all user:* keys
```
</CodeExample>

<WarningBox>

Prefix is required. Trying to flush with an empty string triggers a PHP ArgumentCountError — use flushAll() instead.

</WarningBox>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="flushAll">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function flushAll(): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Unconditionally wipes the entire cache backend by delegating to the driver's flushAll(). Records the operation in profiler.

<WarningBox>

Destroys all cached data across all application contexts sharing this driver

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Triggers immediate re-computation on next read

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Prefer flush('prefix:') in production

</WarningBox>

</ApiMethod>

## Tag Operations

<ApiMethod name="tags">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function tags(array $tags): TaggedRedisDriver
```

</ApiSignature>

Returns a Redis tag-scoped cache proxy for the given tags. Available only when the active driver is RedisDriver.

<ApiParam name="$tags" type="array" required>

Tag identifiers used to scope subsequent cache operations.

</ApiParam>

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
Cache::tags(['users'])->set('user:42:profile', $data, 3600);
Cache::tags(['users'])->flush(); // All entries tagged 'users'
```
</CodeExample>

<ApiThrows type="RuntimeException">

Thrown when the active driver is not RedisDriver.

</ApiThrows>

</ApiMethod>

## Testing Hooks

<ApiMethod name="setDriver">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function setDriver(Driver $driver): void
```

</ApiSignature>

Replaces the active driver instance directly. Use in tests to bypass config-based resolution and external services.

<ApiParam name="$driver" type="driver" required>

Driver implementation used for subsequent cache calls.

</ApiParam>

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
Cache::setDriver(new ArrayDriver());
// ... run tests ...
Cache::reset();
```
</CodeExample>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="reset">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public static function reset(): void
```

</ApiSignature>

Clears the cached driver instance. The next cache call resolves the driver again from config.

</ApiMethod>

<AiContext>
```txt
symbol: Skim\Cache\Cache
role: static cache facade
layer: cache
lifecycle: static facade, driver resolved on first cache call
owns: driver instance cache
flow: Cache::method() -> driver() -> resolveDriver() [primary -> fallback] -> concrete driver -> profiler
entry_points:
  - remember
  - get
  - set
  - has
  - delete
  - flush
  - flushAll
  - tags
config_reads:
  - cache.driver
  - cache.fallback
  - cache.ttl
  - cache.redis.*
  - cache.prefix
  - cache.file.path
invariants:
  - driver is resolved once and reused until reset() or setDriver()
  - get() returns default on miss
  - remember() computes and stores only on miss
  - tags() requires RedisDriver
  - flush() requires non-empty prefix
side_effects:
  - Profiler::cache records cache operations
  - setDriver() replaces active driver
  - reset() forces re-resolution
non_goals:
  - Does not expose backend-specific APIs except Redis tags
  - Does not handle serialization
  - Fallback protects app availability, not cache consistency guarantees
```
